title: An Adagietto without a fixed pace
question: How does Mengelberg combine a shorter span with flexible phrasing beside the Peabody orchestra’s broader reading?
intro: Yale’s study of Mengelberg’s 1926 Adagietto describes coordinated string portamento, forward-moving pickups and a slower beginning to the returning theme. The supplied Mengelberg transfer measures 7:17 against 10:21 for the existing Peabody recording: these are file lengths, not uniform tempo ratios.
